# Incident Report — STRRAT RAT Infection

**Evidence file:** `2024-07-30-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (11,562 packets, 2024-07-30 06:38:48 – 06:48:34 UTC+4, 585.7 sec)
**No IDS/Suricata alert export was present in the evidence folder** — findings below are derived entirely from packet-level analysis with tshark.

## 1. Victim host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | **172.16.1.66** |
| MAC | **00:1e:64:ec:f3:08** (Intel NIC) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-SKBR25F** |
| Logged-in domain user | **ccollier** |
| OS | Microsoft Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit |
| AV present | Windows Defender only |
| Domain environment | AD domain `wiresharkworkshop.online`, DC = WIRESHARK-WS-DC (172.16.1.4, MAC 5c:f9:dd:8c:97:35) |

Confirmed via NBNS name registrations (`DESKTOP-SKBR25F<00>`, `WIRESHARKWORKSH<00>`), ARP resolution, and Kerberos `CNameString` values (`ccollier`, `DESKTOP-SKBR25F$`) exchanged with the DC.

## 2. Malware family

**STRRAT** (Java-based backdoor/RAT), **version 1.6**.

**Attribution: signature-confirmed, not behavioral.** The malware's own C2 beacon is plaintext and self-identifies literally: the pipe-delimited "ping" message decodes to
```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender|<base64 active-window-title>|1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|<idle-time>
```
sent from the victim to the C2 approximately every 5 seconds throughout the capture (102 beacon packets observed, first at 2024-07-30 06:40:05.95, last at 06:48:34.62). Bot/campaign ID: `1BE8292C`. The base64 field is the active foreground window title (e.g. `Program Manager`, `Documents`, `Pictures`, `Home`, `pounds-formula [Compatibility Mode] - PowerPoint`), consistent with STRRAT's window-tracking/keylogger-context feature.

Note: no malware binary (jar/exe) transfer appears in this capture, so this is confirmed by protocol content, not by file hash.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control:**
- `141.98.10.79:12132` — plaintext custom TCP protocol (no TLS), single long-lived session from victim source port 49754. This is the sole non-standard-port, non-DNS-resolved destination in the entire capture (all other TCP traffic is 443/80/389/445/135/88/139 to legitimate Microsoft/AD/CDN infrastructure). No DNS lookup precedes this connection — the malware connects straight to the IP.

**Supporting/recon indicator:**
- `ip-api.com` (208.95.112.1) — `GET /json/` with UA `Chrome/73.0.3683.86`, response confirms geolocation `US, Texas, Austin`, which is echoed verbatim (`US:United States`) into every subsequent STRRAT beacon. This is a legitimate third-party service abused for victim geolocation/fingerprinting, not dedicated attacker infrastructure.

**Malicious domains:** None. The only externally-contacted IP with no legitimate reverse business purpose is the bare C2 IP `141.98.10.79`; it was never referenced by name/domain in DNS traffic.

**Malicious URLs:** None beyond the ip-api.com recon call above; no attacker-hosted URL, payload-hosting URL, or exfil URL appears in HTTP traffic.

**Transferred files / hashes:** None observed. Only two HTTP objects transit the capture — `connecttest.txt` (Microsoft NCSI check) and the ip-api.com JSON response — both benign. No jar/exe/dll payload, and therefore no SHA256 of a malware sample, is present in this traffic. The infection predates the start of this capture; only the ongoing beacon activity of an already-installed STRRAT instance is visible.

## 4. Bottom line

Host **DESKTOP-SKBR25F (172.16.1.66)**, logged in as **ccollier**, is actively compromised with **STRRAT v1.6**, beaconing every ~5 seconds to **141.98.10.79:12132**. Recommend isolating the host, blocking 141.98.10.79/12132 at the perimeter, and forcing a credential reset for `ccollier` given STRRAT's known credential-theft/keylogging capability (this capture does not contain the AD account's credentials in cleartext, but the malware's own capability set warrants the reset as a precaution).
